hints: Find the side length: $PQ = |4 - (-2)| = 6$. Midpoint of base is $M(1, 0)$.
In an equilateral triangle of side $s = 6$, the height is $h = s \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 6 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 3\sqrt{3}$.
Since $R$ lies directly above $M(1, 0)$, its coordinates are $R(1, 3\sqrt{3})$.
walkthrough:
Splitting an equilateral triangle creates two equal right triangles.
Find the side length and midpoint of base $PQ$:
$$PQ = |4 - (-2)| = 6$$
$$M = \left(\dfrac{-2 + 4}{2}, 0\right) = (1, 0)$$

Calculate the altitude $h$ of the equilateral triangle and state coordinates of $R$:
$$h = \sqrt{6^2 - 3^2} = \sqrt{36 - 9} = \sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}$$
Since $R$ lies above the $x$-axis on the perpendicular line $x = 1$, $R = (1, 3\sqrt{3})$.

hints: Use the standard triangle area formula: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Simplify to get the exact area $9\sqrt{3}$.
walkthrough:
Splitting an equilateral triangle creates two equal right triangles.
Apply the area formula with base $PQ = 6$ and altitude $h = 3\sqrt{3}$:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times h = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3\sqrt{3}$$
